title: Community Helpers

themePack.overview: Toddlers meet everyday helpers—teachers, doctors, firefighters, mail carriers, and builders—through short imitation games, parallel dramatic play, and oversized props. Experiences stay brief and concrete: try on a hat, deliver one letter, gently check a teddy, then move on. Unlike preschool community units, this week emphasizes parallel play, simple thank-you language, and large materials rather than maps, interviews, or multi-step workshops.
themePack.materials:
Helper dress-up hats (firefighter, builder, doctor—toddler-sized)
Toy stethoscope and soft bandage rolls
Soft hose prop / short pool noodle section
Toy mailbags and large envelopes
Mailbox prop with wide slot
Friend photo cards for deliveries
Helper picture cards
Large soft blocks and toy trucks
Toy tools (chunky, no sharp edges)
Stuffed animals for rescue/clinic play
Washable paint, sponges, and large thank-you cardstock
Scarves for parade waves
Floor mats and clear parade path markers
themePack.family: On walks or errands, point out one helper you see—“The mail carrier brings letters” or “The nurse helps people feel better.” At home, invite your toddler to pretend-check a stuffed animal or deliver a drawing to a family member. Practice saying thank you together for helpers who care for your family.
milestones: Language: Names or points to familiar helpers and uses help/thank-you words with support
SEL: Shows caring actions in pretend play (gentle checkup, soft rescue) and practices gratitude
Motor: Carries oversized props, posts large envelopes, marches in a short parade, and stacks large blocks
Cognition: Matches a helper tool to a helper role in simple one-step games

songs.title: Helpers Help Us Chant
songs.lyrics:
Helpers help us every day,
Wave hello and on our way.
Hats and tools and caring hands,
Thank you, helpers, in our land.
songs.motions: Wave; tip an imaginary hat; show open caring hands; blow a thank-you kiss or wave at the end.
songs.teacherDirections: Hold one helper card per verse repetition. Keep to two minutes. Invite toddlers to choose a hat to hold while chanting—no need for full costumes.
songs.whenToUse: Opening circle and Thank You Helpers Parade Prep
songs.transitionPurpose: Introduce helper vocabulary and gratitude language

songs.title: Stop and Go Helpers
songs.lyrics:
Green means go, we help and roll,
Red means stop—we self-control.
Helpers watch and keep us safe,
Stop and go at helper pace.
songs.motions: March or slow scooter roll on green; freeze on red; hands on hips as proud helpers on safe.
songs.teacherDirections: Pair with Police Officer Stop and Go using large red/green signs. Keep speeds walking-slow. Celebrate freezes enthusiastically.
songs.whenToUse: Gross-motor helper games and outdoor transitions
songs.transitionPurpose: Practice body control with helper framing

songs.title: Thank You March
songs.lyrics:
March, march, thank you feet,
Smile at helpers down the street.
Doctor, teacher, firefighter too,
Thank you, thank you—we thank you!
songs.motions: March in place or along a short path; point to helper cards as named; big thank-you wave on the final line.
songs.teacherDirections: Use for Helper Hats Parade. Call only 2–3 helper names. End with bows—short and joyful.
songs.transitionPurpose: Celebrate helpers and close the week with gratitude

books.title: Whose Hands Are These?
books.author: Miranda Paul
books.why: Rhythmic clues about helping hands invite toddlers to guess helper jobs without long text.
before: Who helps with their hands in our community?
during: What job might these hands do?
after: Whose helping hands do you want to thank today?
books.substitute: Helper picture cards with Helpers Help Us Chant if the book is out.

books.title: Helpers in My Community
books.author: Bobbie Kalman
books.why: Clear community photos support simple naming and matching of toddler-familiar helpers.
before: Let’s find a helper we know.
during: Point to the helper’s tool or hat.
after: Which helper would you like to pretend to be?
books.substitute: Photo walk of school helpers (director, cook, custodian) with thank-you waves.

books.title: Career Day
books.author: Anne Rockwell
books.why: Friendly classroom career visit scenes connect helper roles to kids’ everyday world.
before: What job do you wonder about?
during: What is this helper doing to care for people?
after: How can we say thank you to school helpers?
books.substitute: Thank-You Helper Cards process art plus oral thank-yous to classroom adults.

printableIdeas.title: Toddler Helper Picture Card Pack
printableIdeas.purpose: Large single-helper cards for discovery basket labeling, stop-and-go cues, and parade naming—kept simpler than preschool multi-step job maps.

printableIdeas.title: Thank You Helper Card Templates
printableIdeas.purpose: Oversized blank cards with a printed Thank You banner for sponge-paint gratitude art.

teacherTips: Offer 3–4 oversized props only; name one helper at a time.
Expect parallel exploration more than group discussion.
Model gentle touch on stuffed animals first; keep turns short.
Differentiate from preschool clinics—no charts/forms; just care actions.
Emphasize helping, not scary emergencies; soft hose only.
Walking pace only; clear collision paths; helmets if ride-ons are used.
Process art focus—sponge prints celebrate gratitude without identical products.
Large blocks only; no climbing towers; spot lifting outdoors.

themePack.safetyNotes: Use chunky, washable props without sharp tools or realistic scary emergency themes. Supervise dress-up to prevent trip hazards from oversized costumes—prefer hats over full suits. Ride-on stop-and-go stays slow with clear paths. Outdoor building uses soft/large blocks only. Paint activities need smocks and mouthing supervision. Keep play inclusive: helpers of many genders and roles are represented in photos and props.

notes: Explicitly differentiated from preschool Community Helpers: shorter turns, imitation/parallel play, oversized props, no maps/thank-you workshops with writing demands. Original helper chants preferred over bus/pop songs. Avoid duplicating discovery-basket wording from sensory weeks by focusing on helper-tool matching.
